afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 062352
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
452 PM MST Fri Nov 6 2026

.UPDATE...Updated 00Z Aviation Discussion.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Major waterways such as the Salt and Gila Rivers will continue
  to experience elevated flows through at least the weekend due 
  to dam releases.

- With the exception of a slight chances of showers and 
  thunderstorms over parts of south-central and eastern Arizona 
  this afternoon, dry weather will be common through at least the 
  middle of next week. 

- Temperatures will warm toward near and slightly above normal 
  levels for the weekend and into next week.

  
&&

.SHORT TERM /Today through Sunday/... 
A cut-off low, currently spinning over Arizona and northern Mexico 
will be the focal point for the most appreciable weather changes 
observed since the beginning of this week. This feature, along 
with orographic influences, have already set off some light shower
activity this morning over eastern Arizona, but rain chances for 
this area will extend into this afternoon and evening, with 
perhaps the lower deserts even seeing a stray shower or two. 
Available moisture is not overly impressive, with PWATs around 
0.5-0.7" (though this is still 150-200% of normal for this time 
of year) so most activity during this timeframe, much like the 
morning, should be fairly light. However, boundary-level mixing 
ratios are currently around 6-7 g/kg, which, combined with day- 
time heating, should be sufficient enough to generate at least 
some modest MLCAPE around 250-500 J/kg, enough to promote some 
isolated thunderstorms that could yield some higher rainfall 
rates. As for the above-mentioned lower desert rainfall, as the 
cold-core dives further south, it will help to pull moisture back 
toward south-central Arizona which could yield some sprinkles or 
light showers over areas such as the Phoenix metro, but chances 
are only around 10-20%. Accumulations will generally be anywhere 
from a few hundredths to around a tenth of an inch, with some 
locally higher totals under any heavier shower/storms that can
develop.

Higher momentum northerly flow aloft over the lower Colorado 
River Valley and SE California, a product of the interaction 
between our regional low and eastern Pacific ridging, will result 
in some breezy conditions this afternoon and into Saturday morning 
for those above-listed areas. Gusts 20-30 mph will be common for 
lower elevation locations while ridgetops can expect occasionally 
higher gusts. As the high shifts further east as we transition
into the weekend, surface pressure rises will help generate some 
marginal, but seasonally common, nocturnal/morning breeziness for 
portions of south-central Arizona. Readings 15-25 mph appear to be
the most likely outcome with typical locally higher gusts around 
prominent terrain features. 

After another afternoon with temperatures near or just below 
seasonal norms today, the aforementioned Pacific anti-cyclone will
provide us a bit of warming for Saturday and Sunday. Forecasted 
afternoon highs for this timeframe have ticked up a degree or two 
over the past few forecast periods and now range generally in the 
upper 70s to mid 80s for the lower elevations, with mid 60s to mid
70s being common for higher terrain areas. These will likely be 
the first widespread above-normal values we see so far this 
November, but by only exceeding seasonal levels by about 3-5 
degrees, the weekend should be quite pleasant regionwide. 

&&

.LONG TERM /Monday through Thursday/... 
With northern stream jet energy retreating towards the Canadian 
border under broad ridging, several weak low amplitude features 
will align in the southern stream over northern Mexico during the 
first half of the week before large scale hemispheric pattern 
amplification becomes a dominating feature. Predominant anti- 
cyclonic flow will continue to promote surface pressure rises over
the intermountain West and dry N/NE boundary layer flow. The vast
majority of ensemble membership keeps any notable shortwave 
ascent removed from the CWA, and confidence is very good that dry 
conditions will prevail through at least the middle of the week. 
With H5 heights remaining nearly constant in a 580-584dm range, 
forecast numerical spread is rather narrow indicating very good 
confidence in a persistence type forecast and readings very near 
climatology. Ensemble spread grows markedly towards the end of 
next week as pronounced northern stream pattern amplification 
driven largely by an unusual early season sudden stratospheric 
warming (SSW) event unfolds. The perturbation of the polar vortex 
should cause poleward ridge retrogression while deep negative 
height anomalies descend equatorward into the NE Conus and Pacific
NW. While operational models are consistent in focusing strong 
jet energy and Pacific moisture towards northern California with 
inconsequential shortwave energy into the Southwest, there is a 
non- trivial amount of NAEFS members suggesting much deeper, 
intense troughing moving into the local area next weekend. Given 
this amplification phase, continued wide ensemble spread and 
potentially large variations in operational models yielding low 
forecast confidence should be expected into next week. 

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 2350Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT: 
The main aviation weather issues will be low confidence on wind
directions, especially late this afternoon through this evening,
and a period with low chances (10-30%) of VCSH/SHRA conditions
mainly focused to the east and north of the Phoenix airspace
between 00-07Z. Winds will overall favor E to NE directions,
however, directions may temporarily favor NW this evening (low to
moderate confidence). Speeds should be fairly light through
tonight, AOB 8 kts sustained. However, if virga or SHRA develops
near the terminals, winds could become briefly gusty (gusts up to
20 kts) and erratic. TEMPO BKN decks between 060-090 may also
develop while virga/SHRA is present in/near the Phoenix airspace.
Overnight, winds above the surface will increase out of the east,
causing a minor LLWS concern, but it is expected to remain below
TAF thresholds. A surge of easterly winds with sustained speeds
between 8-12 kts and gusts into the middle to upper teens is then
expected Saturday by mid to late morning. The easterly winds will
continue through the end of the TAF period and a typical westerly
shift is not expected tomorrow afternoon or evening. 

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH: 
Wind gusts are starting to die off, but a few occasional gusts of
15-20 kt are possible over the next couple of hours. Wind speeds
will then go aob 10 kt at KIPL, but remain elevated around 10-15 
kt at KBLH through the rest of the period. Directions will 
predominately be out of the NW at KIPL and out of the N at BLH. 
Skies will remain mostly clear. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
A few isolated showers or thunderstorms may impact higher terrain 
areas north and east of Phoenix today, however wetting rainfall 
chances are minimal. Otherwise, dry conditions will prevail across 
the region through at least the middle of next week. Minimum 
afternoon humidity levels will largely fall into a 20-30% range in 
western districts and 30-50% in eastern districts. This will follow 
fair to good overnight recovery in western districts and good to 
excellent levels in eastern districts. Northerly winds gusts 20-30 
mph will be common in western districts this afternoon through 
Saturday, while a period of enhanced morning easterly winds will 
develop over Arizona early next week. Outside of these time frames, 
wind speeds will be light with limited gustiness. 

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...None.
CA...None.
&&

$$

SHORT TERM...RW
LONG TERM...18 
AVIATION...Whittock/Berislavich 
FIRE WEATHER...18
